claims.text: A machine-learning surrogate potential trained on a sparse set of ab initio configurations can evaluate the potential-energy surface efficiently.
Combining the surrogate potential with umbrella sampling or metadynamics will accurately sample solid and fluid free-energy landscapes.
Periodic on-the-fly ab initio reweighting will restore electron–vibration coupling effects missed by the surrogate potential.
The hybrid method will produce chemically accurate free energies for both solid and fluid phases.
The hybrid method will reduce computational cost by 10–100 times relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The initial target systems are elemental and binary metals near their melting points.
The method is planned for extension to multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Enhanced sampling will accurately probe free-energy barriers and entropy contributions.
Machine-learning-driven dynamics will rapidly sample configurational space.
Machine-learning-driven dynamics will capture vibrational entropy.
Machine-learning-driven dynamics will capture anharmonic effects.
The hybrid scheme will reproduce phase free-energy differences without incurring the full cost of ab initio molecular dynamics.
Phase free-energy differences will deviate from full ab initio molecular-dynamics results by no more than a few meV per atom.
Predicted melting temperatures will closely agree with full ab initio molecular-dynamics results.
Predicted latent heats will closely agree with full ab initio molecular-dynamics results.
The method will scale more favorably than TOR-TILD for multicomponent systems.
Applicability is limited initially to the high-temperature fusion regime near and above melting.
Applicability below the fusion regime and in systems with extreme electronic complexity is unresolved.
